title: What Are HTML & CSS? 🤔
description: Understand the roles of HTML and CSS with a house‑building analogy.

slides.title: The Web as a House 🏠
slides.content:
# Building a Website = Building a House

Imagine you want to build a house. You need:
- **HTML** = The structure: walls, roof, rooms, doors. It defines what **exists**.
- **CSS** = The decoration: paint colours, curtains, furniture arrangement. It defines **how it looks**.

Just like a house needs both a solid frame and beautiful design, a website uses HTML for content and CSS for presentation.

slides.title: What Exactly is HTML? 🧱
slides.content:
# HTML – HyperText Markup Language - A **markup language** (not a programming language) that tells the browser what each piece of content is. - Uses **tags** (like `

`, `

`) to label headings, paragraphs, images, etc. - Every website you visit is built with HTML at its core. Even complex apps like YouTube render HTML in the end. - HTML is **the skeleton** of the web.

quizData.question: Which analogy best describes HTML's role?

options.text: The blueprint and framing of the house

quizData.explanation: HTML provides the structure and defines what content exists, just like a house's frame.

slides.title: What About CSS? 🎨
slides.content:
# CSS – Cascading Style Sheets

- CSS is the language that styles HTML. It controls colours, fonts, spacing, layout, and animations.
- **Separation of concerns:** HTML handles content, CSS handles appearance. This makes sites easier to maintain.
- Without CSS, every website would look like a plain text document.
- With CSS, you can transform the same HTML into a beautiful blog, a dashboard, or a landing page.

quizData.question: CSS is used to define the structure of a webpage.
quizData.explanation: CSS defines style and layout. HTML defines structure.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Remember the duo

HTML and CSS are always used together. Even when you use a website builder, under the hood it's generating HTML and CSS. Understanding these two languages gives you full creative control!

slides.title: How Do They Work Together? ⚙️
slides.content:
# Linking CSS to HTML

There are three ways:
1. **Inline** – style directly on an HTML element (not recommended).
2. **Internal** – a `<style>` block inside the HTML `<head>`.
3. **External** – a separate `.css` file linked with `<link>` (best practice).

We'll explore all of these later, but for now just know that they're partners!

quizData.question: Which is the most recommended way to add CSS to an HTML page?
quizData.explanation: External stylesheets keep HTML and CSS separate, making your code cleaner and reusable.
